rationale: This is the archive's gen-0 "Distressed external financing intensity" with a winsorization wrapper — a purely cosmetic scaling variant of an already-evaluated signal, and since the portfolio sort is rank-based the winsorization will barely move the alpha it is meant to preserve.

Replacing two hard indicators with a continuous leverage×coverage rank product is a legitimate structural fix to the thin-long-leg diagnosis rather than a relabeling, though the core net-debt-retirement leg remains close to the known net-debt-issuance anomaly and the non-negative weights mean identification comes largely from levered issuers on the short side.

The expected sign is inverted relative to the well-documented positive payout-yield/shareholder-yield anomaly and is justified only by a statistically weak gen-0 result (ls_talpha=-1.39) on a different variable (payout *change*), which reads as sign-fishing; it also asserts the opposite sign to proposal 6 on essentially the same payout-under-distress channel.

Decomposing the contradictory gen-0 chronic-loss financing signal into its debt leg is a genuine diagnostic test of which flow carries the distress interaction, with a coherent sign; the main caveat is that the 0–3 loss-streak multiplier zeroes out most firms, reproducing the sparse-leg problem the author criticized in proposal 2.

target_name: Forced equity issuance without a liquidity buffer
rationale: Swapping the conditioning axis from solvency/profitability to short-term liquidity shortfall (che/lct, wcap/at) is a substantively different mechanism test not covered by the archive, and the sign is internally consistent, though the base sstk/at leg overlaps materially with the known net-share-issuance anomaly so the interaction must be shown to add beyond it.

Because the three-year dividend-payer count is nearly binary and the SUMRANK weight is non-negative, the composite's cross-sectional variation is dominated by the distress rank itself among payers, so the sort largely reproduces the known distress/dividend-payer effects rather than isolating the claimed certification interaction.
